source: JZ Mock D · Paper 2 · Question 18 · Publisher worked answer
label: JZ Mock D · Paper 2 · Question 18
knowledgePattern: Count zeros of an accumulated absolute-value integral by signed areas
solution:
Write g(x)=x+1−k−|x−1|+|x−k|, with k>1. For 0≤x≤1, g(x)=x; for 1≤x≤k, g(x)=2−x; for x≥k, g(x)=x+2−2k.

Let F(y)=∫0yg(x)dx. We always have F(0) = 0. If 1<k≤2, the integrand is positive for positive x apart from possible isolated zeros, so there are no further roots.

For k>2, the integrand is positive up to 2, negative from 2 to 2k−2, and positive afterwards. Thus F first increases, then decreases, then increases without bound.

The accumulated positive area up to 2 is 1. The negative lobe is a triangle of width 2(k−2) and depth k−2, so the minimum of F is 1−(k−2)2.

Exactly two additional positive roots occur when this minimum is strictly negative: k>3. At k = 3 the curve only touches zero once after the origin; for smaller k it does not reach zero again. Hence exactly three distinct nonnegative y-values occur precisely for k>3. Answer B.

hints.title: Remove the absolute values on the correct intervals
hints.body: Split the nonnegative x-axis at the zeros of the two expressions inside the absolute values. Write the linear integrand on each interval.
hints.recap: For absolute-value expressions, use a complete case split and assign every boundary to a valid case.
hints.pitfall: The sign of the whole integrand may change somewhere other than an absolute-value breakpoint.
hints.pause: Simplify each piece and check that adjacent expressions agree at the join.

recall.reminder: For absolute-value expressions, use a complete case split and assign every boundary to a valid case.

hints.title: Track the accumulated area
hints.body: Use the sign of the integrand to decide where the integral from zero increases or decreases.
hints.recap: The derivative of an accumulated integral is its integrand.
hints.pitfall: A zero integrand is a stationary point of the accumulated function, not automatically a zero of that function.
hints.pause: Locate the possible maximum and minimum of the accumulated function.

recall.reminder: The derivative of an accumulated integral is its integrand.

hints.title: Compare the positive and negative areas
hints.body: Calculate the positive area before any negative lobe, and the area removed by that lobe. Determine when the accumulated minimum lies below, on or above zero.
hints.recap: Turning heights, monotonic intervals and endpoint values determine distinct crossings.
hints.pitfall: Count the origin and distinguish a touching root from two crossings.
hints.pause: Translate the required number of roots into a strict parameter condition and check equality.

recall.reminder: Turning heights, monotonic intervals and endpoint values determine distinct crossings.
